answer: Time-locked identity lease. Each identity posts a refundable deposit held in a vault, released only after a quiet period in which the account's activity must stay above a lotus threshold of sustained volume; dormant clones bleed holding cost and forgo yield the whole time. Registering during adoption tides multiplies the lock duration, so a burst of fabrication pays peak-duration interest on every unit simultaneously. An attacker forging N identities needs N times the float plus N times the duration, making the hundredth clone costlier in time than the first in cash.
